newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, gold recovers more.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, gold recovers more.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Friday, but gold extended its recovery for the eighth day in a row as funds took profits on more short positions against a backdrop of good demand for bullion.
"Gold recently reached lows that were unsustainable given industry fundamentals and it proved a bear trap," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
"But this rally is impressive, not just because gold has recovered $18.00 an ounce, from three year lows, but because behind it is very good physical demand," he said.
COMEX April gold ended up $1.50 an ounce at $354.10, after seeing an 18 day intraday high at $356.80. Estimated total gold futures volume was 55,000 contracts.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $351.90/40 an ounce compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $353.30 and the New York close Thursday at $350.40/90.

With commodity funds taking profits on short positions, physical gold demand picking up, and the US dollar and US stockmarket both seeing a downward correction this week, some investors were being tempted back into precious metals, traders said.

In data released Friday, total COMEX gold futures open interest plunged a further 5,371 contracts Thursday to 187,077 contracts, a fall of 12,641 lots in the past week, suggesting the rally was being driven by heavy shortcovering by funds, analysts said.

Short term implied lease rates for gold remained at the lowest levels in some months Friday, around 1.28 percent for the one month rate, also suggesting short positions were being unwound, traders said.
The rally has driven nearby active COMEX gold futures to a rare $2.00 an ounce premium over spot gold bullion prices, traders noted.

But investment demand was picking up also, with purchases of American Eagle gold bullion coins in January, at 51,250 ounces, running at five times the level in January last year, industry consultants CPM Group said.

Spot gold prices were at five year highs around $417.00 an ounce in early 1996, but fell to three year lows around $336.00 an ounce in early 1997, prompting some bargain hunting by investors, analysts noted.
"There's been something of a squeeze on physical precious metal markets of late," another bullion dealer said.
"Physical gold has been leaving the US at a much higher rate than in the past year to take advantage of premiums available elsewhere around 50 cent an ounce," he said.
"Spot gold could get back up to around $360-370 which is probably its equilibrium level in next few months, in a move that would be the mirror image of the trend this time last year."

Spot gold's five-day (weekly) simple moving-average cross back above its 21-day (monthly) moving average at the close Friday, for the first time since November, suggesting the year-long downtrend may be bottoming out, analysts said.
But spot gold would need to climb well above its 55-day (quarterly) moving-average, currently at $356.00, for a convincing end to the downtrend, traders said.
COMEX March silver ended down 4.0 cents though at $5.190 an ounce, after running into resistance near last week's high at $5.275.

Silver had been leading the recovery in the precious metals complex, but this week silver's upward momentum waned, with the spot gold/silver ratio recovering further to 67.8 Friday, after seeing a 21 month low at 65.6 last Friday.
The unwinding of large platinum/gold was spreads was also supporting the gold price, analysts said.
The April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ended little changed around $19.60 an ounce Friday, but the spread has come off the contract highs at $26.60 an ounce seen last week.
NYMEX April platinum ended up $2.10 at $374.90 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium closed up $3.00 at $139.00.

"Last week's heavy selling of palladium put options saw palladium correct down from the nine month highs around $141.00, but support has come back in around $131.00, and there's clearly a supply problem with palladium sponge being quoted at $5.00-6.00 differentials to the plate," one platinum group metals dealer said.
Palladium supplies have been affected by the breakdown in Russian/Japanese contract talks which are due to resume in March, but hedge fund activity in the palladium market has also been reported.
"Russia, the world's largest palladium producer, is just not supplying anyone, putting pressure on palladium sponge in particular," another trade house dealer said.
